parts.t: Zoning and plan designations can be different for each lot.
Delta Council adopted the Official Community Plan 2024, “Housing Our Future” (Bylaw No. 8400), on July 8, 2024.

The OCP gives the commercial village at Annieville its own development permit area (ND3). The City says the village has a special character and provides local services, and that new buildings there should sit close to River Road.
The North Delta Area Plan (revised March 2015) welcomes residential infill on smaller lots east of 116 Street between 90 and 96 Avenue. Outside the areas it names, it does not encourage more density.

Near 88 Avenue and 119 Street, the same plan describes the Kennedy area as a place for shops, services and housing. A 14-storey building went up there in the 1980s, and the plan says more high-rise building would be encouraged. It describes the Kennedy Heights Mall site as large, with room to redevelop.
The MLS® map does not name this area, so ask me about a specific address.

Delta changed its zoning in 2024 so that many single detached and duplex lots can have a secondary suite plus up to two detached suites (a garden suite or coach house). The rules differ by lot, so ask me or the City about an address.
From MLS® sales data (not an official source): the median lot size of detached houses sold from July 1 to October 8, 2026 was 6,840 square feet, across 11 sales with a recorded lot size.
Check the river bank and any slope.

The OCP says the Fraser River waterfront, river bank and ravine slopes in its Fraser River Escarpment area (ND1) are subject to erosion and land slip. If a home is near the river or a slope, ask the City about the exact lot.
Ask the City what the plans allow on the lots around the home, especially near the River Road village, 116 Street and the Kennedy area.
Use the Delta School District school locator for the exact address.
